title: Conditional-testing derivation of fuzzy-extractor impossibility bounds
summary: Determine whether conditional independence testing can recover the unknown-distribution fuzzy-extractor impossibility guarantees of two source theorems.

formal_statement.body: For the unknown-distribution fuzzy-extractor model and the source-defined joint variables $(W,W',Z)$, use the cited conditional independence testing upper-bound framework to derive analogues of the impossibility guarantees in Theorems 5.1 and 6.1 throughout their parameter regimes, or prove an obstruction showing that this framework cannot establish those guarantees.

scope.domain: Unknown-distribution fuzzy extractors and conditional independence testing bounds
assumptions: The fuzzy-extractor model and joint distributions are those of the source
The target guarantees are the impossibility regimes of source Theorems 5.1 and 6.1
Theorem 5.1 uses the source's perfect-correctness regime with $\delta=0$ and $\kappa\ge 3$
Theorem 6.1 uses the source's error-tolerant regime with $\delta\le 1/25$ and $\kappa>0$
The derivation must use the cited conditional independence testing framework
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later fuzzy-extractor impossibility results establish different distributional-advice bounds, but no inspected work derives both source theorem regimes through conditional independence testing or proves that such a derivation is impossible.

progress.summary: The source asks whether conditional independence testing can reproduce its two unknown-distribution impossibility theorems.
